[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Ignoring Files with .gitignore in Git"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"The .gitignore file is a powerful tool in Git that allows you to specify intentionally untracked files that Git should ignore. This prevents sensitive data, build artifacts, or other unnecessary files from being committed to your repository. Using .gitignore keeps your repository clean and focused on the essential source code and project files."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Creating a .gitignore File"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"To create a .gitignore file, simply create a new text file named '.gitignore' in the root directory of your Git repository. This file should be plain text and can be created using any text editor."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"# Example .gitignore file
node_modules/
dist/
*.log
.DS_Store
config.js"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"Syntax and Rules"},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Each line in the .gitignore file specifies a pattern. Git will ignore files and directories that match these patterns."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Blank lines are ignored."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Lines starting with '#' are treated as comments."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Standard glob patterns like '*' (matches zero or more characters), '?' (matches one character), and '[]' (matches a character in the range) are supported."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"A leading slash '/' matches the directory root. For example, '/foo' only ignores 'foo' in the root directory."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"A trailing slash '/' indicates a directory. For example, 'foo/' ignores the directory 'foo' and all its contents."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"A double asterisk '**' matches directories recursively. For example, '**/foo' ignores 'foo' in any subdirectory."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"A leading '! ' negates the pattern. It's possible to re-include a file that was previously excluded."},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Common Use Cases"},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Ignoring build artifacts (e.g., 'dist/', 'build/')"},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Ignoring dependency directories (e.g., 'node_modules/', 'vendor/')"},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Ignoring log files (e.g., '*.log')"},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Ignoring operating system specific files (e.g., '.DS_Store', 'Thumbs.db')"},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Ignoring configuration files containing sensitive information (e.g., 'config.js', 'secrets.env')"},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Ignoring Already Tracked Files"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"If you add a file to .gitignore after it has already been tracked by Git, Git will continue to track it. To stop tracking the file, you need to remove it from the index using the following command:"},{"order":23,"type":"code","text":"git rm --cached <file>"},{"order":24,"type":"paragraph","text":"Then, commit the changes to your repository:"},{"order":25,"type":"code","text":"git commit -m "Stop tracking <file>""},{"order":26,"type":"paragraph","text":"After this, Git will ignore the file as specified in .gitignore."},{"order":27,"type":"subheading","text":"Global .gitignore"},{"order":28,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can also create a global .gitignore file that applies to all your Git repositories on your system. To configure a global .gitignore file, use the following command:"},{"order":29,"type":"code","text":"git config --global core.excludesfile ~/.gitignore_global"},{"order":30,"type":"paragraph","text":"Then, create the '~/.gitignore_global' file and add the patterns you want to ignore globally."},{"order":31,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices"},{"order":32,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always include a .gitignore file in your repository."},{"order":33,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Start with a basic .gitignore file based on your project's technology stack (e.g., using a template from GitHub's gitignore repository)."},{"order":34,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Regularly review and update your .gitignore file as your project evolves."},{"order":35,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Avoid committing sensitive information to your repository by properly configuring your .gitignore file."}]
